# PileUpLock — the pile-up: when one runner can be freed while the rest are together

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

Runners go round a track of length one, each with its own lap time. Pick one runner as the target and call the rest the pack. The pack is together at the start exactly at the multiples of its combined cycle (the least common multiple of the pack's lap times), the same way the wheels' combined cycle works. At those moments the target stands only on a set of evenly spaced spots, as many as the target's lap time divided by its greatest common factor with the combined cycle. The target is freed by the pile-up if and only if its lap time does not divide the combined cycle; then it stands at least a third of a lap from the pack, enough for any field of three or more runners. When the lap time does divide the cycle (the target is locked), no moment with the whole pack at the start separates it. The same holds with the pack together at any shared point, using the greatest common factor of the pack's speed differences. Original to this project (Geo's pile-up idea, 2026). Settled limit, recorded so it is not re-argued: locked targets are the usual case (about 70 percent of small sets with three runners, about 99 percent with six, and every runner of the consecutive-speed sets from four runners on), so this node frees only some runners and is not a route to the whole conjecture by itself. Times are fractions; the usual statement with real times is equivalent (a classical fact, not proved here). This node also holds the shared vocabulary of the Lonely Runner family (far, lonely_at, has_lonely_time, and lonely_runner_upto as a named hypothesis). As proved, differs from the plan: the count of the target's spots (target_spots_count) is not stated, and freed_third_lap is part of pile_up_frees_iff; the pack is any finite family of speeds, so the same claims cover the empty pack and packs with repeated speeds.

## Claims

<a id="pack_together_iff"></a>
### `pack_together_iff`

All the pack is at the start at a fractional time exactly when the denominator divides the greatest common factor of the pack's speeds times the numerator.

```lean
/-- **When the pack is together at the start.** For pack runners indexed by
`P` with speeds `sp`, all are at the start at the time `k / m` exactly when `m`
divides the greatest common factor of their speeds times `k`. -/
def pack_together_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (P : Finset ι) (sp : ι → ℤ) (m : ℕ) (k : ℤ),
    (∀ i ∈ P, (m : ℤ) ∣ sp i * k) ↔ (m : ℤ) ∣ P.gcd sp * k
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.PileUpLock.pack_together_iff_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean)

<a id="locked_never_separated"></a>
### `locked_never_separated`

If the target's speed is a multiple of the pack's greatest common factor, the target is at the start whenever the whole pack is.

```lean
/-- **A locked target is never separated by a pile-up.** If the target's speed
`u` is a multiple of the greatest common factor of the pack's speeds, then at
every moment when the whole pack is at the start, so is the target. -/
def locked_never_separated : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (P : Finset ι) (sp : ι → ℤ) (u : ℤ) (m : ℕ) (k : ℤ), 0 < m →
    (∀ i ∈ P, (m : ℤ) ∣ sp i * k) → P.gcd sp ∣ u → (u * k) % (m : ℤ) = 0
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.PileUpLock.locked_never_separated_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean)

<a id="pile_up_frees_iff"></a>
### `pile_up_frees_iff`

Some moment has the whole pack at the start and the target at least a third of a lap away exactly when the target's speed is not a multiple of the pack's greatest common factor.

```lean
/-- **The pile-up frees exactly the unlocked targets.** Some moment has the
whole pack at the start and the target at least a third of a lap away if and
only if the target's speed is not a multiple of the greatest common factor of
the pack's speeds. A third of a lap is enough for any field of three or more
runners. -/
def pile_up_frees_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (P : Finset ι) (sp : ι → ℤ) (u : ℤ),
    (∃ m : ℕ, ∃ k : ℤ, 0 < m ∧ (∀ i ∈ P, (m : ℤ) ∣ sp i * k) ∧ far 3 m (u * k)) ↔
      ¬ P.gcd sp ∣ u
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.PileUpLock.pile_up_frees_iff_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean)

<a id="shared_point_pile_up"></a>
### `shared_point_pile_up`

The same with the pack together at any shared point: speeds measured relative to one speed, the target is freed exactly when its relative speed is not a multiple of the greatest common factor of the pack's relative speeds.

```lean
/-- **Pile-up at a shared point.** Measuring every speed relative to a pack
speed `a`: some moment has the whole pack together at one point and the target
at least a third of a lap from it if and only if the target's relative speed
is not a multiple of the greatest common factor of the pack's relative speeds. -/
def shared_point_pile_up : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (P : Finset ι) (sp : ι → ℤ) (a u : ℤ),
    (∃ m : ℕ, ∃ k : ℤ, 0 < m ∧ (∀ i ∈ P, (m : ℤ) ∣ (sp i - a) * k) ∧
        far 3 m ((u - a) * k)) ↔
      ¬ P.gcd (fun i => sp i - a) ∣ (u - a)
```

**Rests on:** [`PileUpLock.pile_up_frees_iff`](PileUpLock.md#pile_up_frees_iff)

**Proof:** `RNS.PileUpLock.shared_point_pile_up_step` in [`RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/PileUpLock.lean)
